subject: Machining + Metrology + CIM
summary: a full revision of machining (chip types, shear-plane stress, the extended Taylor equation, drilling MRR), machine tools (gear hobbing and shaping, milling time), non-traditional machining (EDM dielectric, electron beam drilling, electrochemical grinding), metrology (ISO fits, accuracy and precision, process capability) and CIM (SCARA robots, Bézier curves)

questions.text: Titanium alloys machined at moderate to high cutting speeds usually produce serrated (saw-tooth, segmented) chips. The main reason is
opts: their high thermal conductivity
their low thermal conductivity, which concentrates heat in narrow shear bands (adiabatic shear) where the metal softens and shears in bursts
their very low hardness
the formation of a stable built-up edge
questions.ans: (B) their low thermal conductivity, which concentrates heat in narrow shear bands (adiabatic shear) where the metal softens and shears in bursts
solution: Concept: Chip type depends on the work material and cutting conditions: continuous (ductile), discontinuous (brittle), with BUE (low speed, adhesive), serrated (thermoplastic instability).
Titanium conducts heat poorly, so the heat of shearing stays in a thin band; the local softening exceeds strain hardening and shear localises periodically.
The same makes the tool tip run very hot, which is why titanium is cut at low speeds with sharp, positive-rake carbide tools and plenty of coolant.
Answer: (B)
Exam tip: Serrated chips cause force fluctuations and chatter; hardened steels and nickel alloys give them too.

questions.text: In orthogonal cutting with a tool of rake angle 6°, the uncut chip thickness is 0.25 mm, the width of cut is 2.5 mm and the chip thickness ratio is 0.42. The cutting force is 1000 N and the thrust force is 420 N. The mean shear stress on the shear plane (in MPa, round off to the nearest integer) is ______
solution: Concept: Shear angle from tan φ = r cos α/(1 − r sin α); shear force Fs = Fc cos φ − Ft sin φ acts on the shear-plane area As = tw/sin φ.
Exam tip: The shear-plane area is larger than the uncut chip area tw by the factor 1/sin φ; forgetting it overestimates τ by about 2.5 times here.

questions.text: In the extended Taylor equation VT<sup>n</sup>f<sup>a</sup>d<sup>b</sup> = C for carbide tools (typically n ≈ 0.25, a ≈ 0.5–0.75, b ≈ 0.15–0.35), the cutting variables arranged in decreasing order of their effect on tool life are
opts: depth of cut > feed > cutting speed
feed > cutting speed > depth of cut
cutting speed > feed > depth of cut
all three have equal effect
questions.ans: (C) cutting speed > feed > depth of cut
solution: Concept: Solving for T: T = C1/n V−1/n f−a/n d−b/n; the larger the exponent, the stronger the effect.
With n = 0.25: exponent of V is 4, of f about 2–3, of d about 0.6–1.4.
So speed has by far the biggest effect, then feed, then depth of cut.
Answer: (C)
Exam tip: For productivity with long tool life, take the largest depth of cut first, then the largest feed, and then choose the speed.

questions.text: A 20 mm diameter twist drill runs at 400 rpm with a feed of 0.2 mm/rev, drilling into solid metal. The material removal rate (in mm³/s, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: In drilling solid metal, MRR = (πD²/4) × feed per minute.
Feed velocity = f N = 0.2 × 400 = 80 mm/min = 1.333 mm/s
Area = π × 20²/4 = 314.16 mm²
Exam tip: For enlarging an existing hole of diameter d0, use π(D² − d0²)/4 instead.

questions.text: Which statement about gear hobbing and gear shaping is correct?
opts: Gear hobbing can cut internal gears and cluster gears close to a shoulder, but gear shaping cannot
Both processes form each tooth space separately with a form cutter and an indexing head
Gear shaping can cut internal gears and gears close to a shoulder, which gear hobbing cannot
Gear shaping is faster than hobbing for long runs of external spur gears
questions.ans: (C) Gear shaping can cut internal gears and gears close to a shoulder, which gear hobbing cannot
solution: Concept: Both are generating processes: the cutter and blank rotate in a fixed ratio, like meshing gears, so one cutter cuts all tooth numbers of a given module.
The hob is a worm-like cutter that needs clearance past the gear face, so it cannot reach internal teeth or teeth close to a shoulder.
The gear-shaper cutter reciprocates like a pinion, so it can cut internal gears and cluster gears; hobbing is faster for external spur and helical gears because cutting is continuous.
Answer: (C)
Exam tip: Form milling with a dividing head is the non-generating method; it needs a different cutter for each range of tooth numbers.

questions.text: A through slot is cut along the full 100 mm length of a block in one pass, as shown, by an end mill of 16 mm diameter with 4 teeth, running at 1200 rpm with a feed of 0.05 mm per tooth. The cutter starts with its edge just touching the block and travels until it has completely cleared the far end. The machining time (in seconds, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: Table feed vf = fz z N; the cutter travel = work length + approach + over-travel.
The cutter centre starts D/2 before the block and must finish D/2 beyond it: travel = 100 + 8 + 8 = 116 mm
Exam tip: For slab milling the approach is √(d(D − d)); for face milling with a centred cutter it is D/2 (or D for a full-width finish).

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the dielectric fluid in electric discharge machining?
opts: Acting as an insulator until the breakdown voltage is reached, then ionising to form the spark channel
Flushing the eroded debris out of the gap
Cooling the electrode and workpiece
Conducting the machining current continuously between tool and work, as an electrolyte does in ECM
questions.ans: (D) Conducting the machining current continuously between tool and work, as an electrolyte does in ECM
solution: Concept: EDM needs a non-conducting fluid (kerosene-based oil or deionised water) so that discrete sparks occur at the closest points.
The dielectric holds off the voltage, then ionises to confine the spark; it quenches and flushes away the molten debris and cools the surfaces.
Continuous conduction would be ECM-like electrolysis, not spark erosion; it would stop the sparking altogether.
Answer: (D)
Exam tip: Poor flushing causes arcing and short circuits; graphite and copper are the usual tool materials.

questions.text: An electron beam of 150 kV and 20 mA drills a hole of 0.5 mm diameter through a steel sheet 2 mm thick. Only 80 % of the beam power is used in removing metal, and the energy needed to remove (melt and vaporise) the steel is 10 J/mm³. The time taken to drill the hole (in milliseconds, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Time = energy needed/useful power; the energy needed = volume × specific removal energy.
Beam power = 150 × 10³ × 20 × 10⁻³ = 3000 W; useful power = 0.8 × 3000 = 2400 W
Volume = π/4 × 0.5² × 2 = 0.3927 mm³ → energy = 3.927 J
Exam tip: EBM needs a vacuum chamber (electrons scatter in air); LBM works in air but metals reflect much of the light.

questions.text: Electrochemical grinding (ECG) is used for sharpening carbide cutting tools. In ECG,
opts: about 90 % or more of the material is removed by electrolytic dissolution, the metal-bonded abrasive wheel mainly scraping away the passive film
the material is removed entirely by the abrasive grains, the electrolyte only cooling the work
the wheel is made the anode and the work the cathode
sparks between the wheel and the work remove the material
questions.ans: (A) about 90 % or more of the material is removed by electrolytic dissolution, the metal-bonded abrasive wheel mainly scraping away the passive film
solution: Concept: ECG combines ECM and grinding: a conductive (metal-bonded diamond) wheel is the cathode and the work the anode, with electrolyte in the gap kept by the protruding grains.
Most of the stock goes by anodic dissolution; the grains remove the oxide film and maintain the gap, so there is little heat, no burrs and very low wheel wear.
Option D describes electro-discharge grinding.
Answer: (A)
Exam tip: ECG is ideal for burr-free, stress-free grinding of hard, conductive materials such as cemented carbides.

questions.text: For an ISO hole designated with the letter H (e.g. 40 H7),
opts: the upper deviation is zero
the lower deviation is zero, so the minimum hole size equals the basic size
the tolerance is symmetrical about the basic size
the fundamental deviation depends on the tolerance grade
questions.ans: (B) the lower deviation is zero, so the minimum hole size equals the basic size
solution: Concept: The letter gives the fundamental deviation (position of the tolerance zone); the number gives the tolerance grade (its width).
For the H hole the fundamental deviation is the lower deviation = 0, so the hole ranges from the basic size to basic size + IT.
Likewise an h shaft has upper deviation 0 (shaft-basis system); JS/js zones are symmetrical.
Answer: (B)
Exam tip: H is the basis of the hole-basis system: one set of reamers and plug gauges serves all the fits.

questions.text: A fit is specified as 40 H7/k6, with the hole 40.000–40.025 mm and the shaft 40.002–40.018 mm. The maximum clearance of the fit (in μm) is ______
solution: Concept: Maximum clearance = largest hole − smallest shaft; maximum interference = largest shaft − smallest hole.
Maximum clearance = 40.025 − 40.002 = 0.023 mm = 23 μm
Maximum interference = 40.018 − 40.000 = 18 μm
Since the fit can give either a clearance or an interference, it is a transition fit.
Exam tip: Draw the two tolerance zones on a line; if they overlap, the fit is a transition fit.

questions.text: A gauge block of true length 25.000 mm is measured ten times with an instrument. The readings are all between 25.041 mm and 25.043 mm. The instrument is
opts: accurate and precise
accurate but not precise
neither accurate nor precise
precise but not accurate, showing a systematic error of about +0.042 mm that can be removed by calibration
questions.ans: (D) precise but not accurate, showing a systematic error of about +0.042 mm that can be removed by calibration
solution: Concept: Precision = closeness of repeated readings to one another (repeatability); accuracy = closeness of the mean reading to the true value.
The spread is only 0.002 mm (high precision), but the mean, about 25.042 mm, is 0.042 mm off the true value (poor accuracy).
A constant offset is a systematic error: it can be found by calibration against a standard and corrected.
Answer: (D)
Exam tip: Random errors set the precision and cannot be calibrated out; systematic errors set the bias and can.

questions.text: A shaft diameter is specified as 50 ± 0.06 mm. The machining process produces diameters that are normally distributed with a mean of 50.02 mm and a standard deviation of 0.01 mm. The process capability index C<sub>pk</sub> (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Cpk = min(USL − μ, μ − LSL)/(3σ); it accounts for the process not being centred, while Cp = (USL − LSL)/(6σ) does not.
Exam tip: Cpk ≥ 1.33 is the usual minimum for a capable process; re-centring this process would raise Cpk to 2.

questions.text: A SCARA robot, widely used for pick-and-place and assembly, has
opts: three prismatic joints at right angles (Cartesian)
two rotary joints with parallel vertical axes and one vertical prismatic joint, giving compliance in the horizontal plane and rigidity vertically
one rotary base joint and two prismatic joints (cylindrical)
six rotary joints (articulated arm)
questions.ans: (B) two rotary joints with parallel vertical axes and one vertical prismatic joint, giving compliance in the horizontal plane and rigidity vertically
solution: Concept: SCARA = Selective Compliance Assembly Robot Arm.

Its two shoulder/elbow joints rotate about parallel vertical axes, so the arm is compliant sideways (helping to insert pins into holes) but stiff vertically; a vertical prismatic axis (plus a wrist roll) does the insertion.
Its work envelope is a thick, kidney-shaped cylinder region.
Answer: (B)
Exam tip: Count joints: Cartesian PPP, cylindrical RPP, spherical (polar) RRP, SCARA RRP with parallel R axes, articulated RRR(+wrist).

questions.text: A cubic Bézier curve has the control points P<sub>0</sub>(0, 0), P<sub>1</sub>(1, 3), P<sub>2</sub>(3, 3) and P<sub>3</sub>(4, 0). The y-coordinate of the point on the curve at parameter u = 0.4 (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: P(u) = (1 − u)³P0 + 3u(1 − u)²P1 + 3u²(1 − u)P2 + u³P3 (Bernstein polynomials; curve below).
At u = 0.4 the weights are 0.216, 0.432, 0.288 and 0.064 (sum = 1).
Exam tip: The curve passes through P0 and P3 only, is tangent to P0P1 and P2P3 at its ends, and stays inside the convex hull of the control points.
